newsitem.title: USA: Stocks hit another record, techs sizzle.
newsitem.headline: Stocks hit another record, techs sizzle.

text.p: Stocks shattered records again Friday as technology issues rallied on hopes the downturn in the computer chip industry had bottomed after an upbeat report from semiconductor equipment maker Applied Materials.
"Techs are on fire. It's a flight to earnings growth," said Philip Orlando of Value Line Asset Management.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 53.29 points to 6,471.76. It was the Dow's 42nd record high for 1996 and the 11th this month. The index added 123.73 for the week.
The New York Stock Exchange imposed curbs on certain programme trading five minutes before the market closed.
In the broader market, advances outpaced declines, 1,497 to 956, on very heavy NYSE volume of 525.2 million shares.
The technology-studded Nasdaq composite index soared 16.28 points or 1.3 percent to 1,274.36, a record. The previous high of 1,270.36 was set Nov. 14. The index added 12.56 for the week.
International Business Machines Corp. surged 4-3/4 to 158-5/8.

While IBM has jumped more than 70 percent from its July low of 90-1/4, Ken Tower, a technical analyst at UST Securities, said it may rise further and that the overall market appeared healthy technically.
Despite the recent explosive rally in equities, Tower said a recent UST study showed many issues had not matched the 18 percent gains in the Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks.

"Out of the 6,000 stocks we follow, 69 percent have underperformed since the July bottom and 32 percent are lower than the July bottom.... It's a broad rally but not a barn burner or a speculative rally from the traditional standpoint," Tower said.

Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage, noted this was a traditionally strong time of the year for the stock market, "so it would be pretty surprising to see any type of tumble here. We have lot of momentum and people are hanging onto the stocks they want. It's a supply-demand question."

One laggard group that rallied on Friday was the semiconductor equipment sector. Industry flagship Applied Materials said that even at the low point in the current cycle, it expects profit margins to remain higher than in previous market cycles, analysts said.

Applied Materials rallied 6-5/8 to 38-5/8 as several brokers raised ratings. KLA Instruments climbed 5-1/4 to 38-1/2, Tencor was up 5-3/4 to 27, Lam Research rose 4-9/16 to 34-1/16, Novellus jumped 9-49/64 to 59-3/4 and PRI Automation was up 6-5/8 to 43-1/8. Intel, the world's largest chip maker, rose 3-5/8 to 122-1/2.
Semiconductor equipment stocks are often seen by investors as bellwethers for the next wave of technology growth.

But custom chip maker VLSI Technology lost 2-3/8 to 22-5/8. It plans to stop production at its San Jose, Calif., wafer fabrication plant by the end of 1997, a move the will result in job cuts and a charge of up to $120 million.
Alrenco, an operator of rental-purchase stores, fell 7-3/4 to 11-3/4 after warning of an earnings shortfall.
Several IPOs attracted interest. Nu Skin Asia Pacific, the exclusive Asian distributor of Nu Skin International personal products, surged 5-3/4 to 28-3/4.
CANTV, the Venezuelan telephone company, climbed 2-7/8 to 25-7/8 in its first day of trading. Rogue Wave Software shares jumped to 14-3/4 from their IPO price of 12.
The S&P 500 climbed 5.98 to 748.73, up 11.11 on the week.
The NYSE Composite index rose 2.41 to 394.66, a record. The average price per share rose 25 cents. The index was up 4.64 on the week.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.01 to 590.77, and added 5.36 on the week.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at 7,210.595, up 53.940 or 0.75 percent. The index rose 82.419 from a week ago.
